title: 277. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Logarithmic Graph Intercepts
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Basic Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_2 x\)?
questions.explanation: The \(x\)-intercept occurs when \(y=0\). Set \(\log_2 x=0\). Since \(\log_2 1=0\), we have \(x=1\). Therefore the \(x\)-intercept is \((1,0)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Set the logarithmic output equal to zero and solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Horizontally Shifted Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_3(x-2)\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(y=0\): \(\log_3(x-2)=0\). Since \(\log_3 1=0\), we need \(x-2=1\). Then \(x=3\). Therefore the \(x\)-intercept is \((3,0)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Set the argument of the logarithm equal to \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the \(y\)-intercept of \(y=\log_b(x+c)\) when \(x=0\) is in the domain.
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_2(x+4)\)?
questions.explanation: The \(y\)-intercept occurs when \(x=0\). Substitute \(x=0\): \(y=\log_2(0+4)=\log_2 4=2\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,2)\), so option A is correct.

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Shifted Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_5(x+1)-1\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(y=0\): \(\log_5(x+1)-1=0\). Then \(\log_5(x+1)=1\). By the definition of logarithm, \(x+1=5^1=5\). Therefore \(x=4\). The \(x\)-intercept is \((4,0)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Rewrite the equation in exponential form after isolating the logarithm.

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Horizontally and Vertically Shifted Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_2(x-1)+1\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(y=0\): \(\log_2(x-1)+1=0\). Then \(\log_2(x-1)=-1\). In exponential form, \(x-1=2^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\). Therefore \(x=\frac{3}{2}\). The \(x\)-intercept is \(\left(\frac{3}{2},0\right)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Isolate the logarithm and convert to exponential form.

questions.concept: Y-Intercept of a Logarithmic Graph with a Constant
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_3(x+9)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=0\): \(y=\log_3(0+9)=\log_3 9\). Since \(3^2=9\), \(\log_3 9=2\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,2)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Evaluate the logarithm at \(x=0\) by expressing the argument as a power of the base.

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Vertically Shifted Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_2(x+7)-3\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(y=0\): \(\log_2(x+7)-3=0\). Then \(\log_2(x+7)=3\). In exponential form, \(x+7=2^3=8\). Therefore \(x=1\). The \(x\)-intercept is \((1,0)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Isolate the logarithm and rewrite it as an exponential equation.

questions.concept: Y-Intercept of a Common Logarithmic Graph
questions.question: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_{10}(x+100)\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x=0\): \(y=\log_{10}(0+100)=\log_{10}100\). Since \(10^2=100\), \(\log_{10}100=2\). Therefore the \(y\)-intercept is \((0,2)\), so option A is correct.

questions.concept: X-Intercept of a Logarithmic Graph with a Linear Argument
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of \(y=\log_4(2x-3)\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(y=0\): \(\log_4(2x-3)=0\). Since \(\log_4 1=0\), we need \(2x-3=1\). Then \(2x=4\), so \(x=2\). The \(x\)-intercept is \((2,0)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Set the argument equal to \(1\) and solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Multiple X-Intercepts of a Logarithmic Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine all \(x\)-intercepts of a logarithmic graph with a quadratic argument.
questions.question: What are the \(x\)-intercepts of the graph of \(y=\log_2(x^2-3x-3)\)?
questions.explanation:
Set \(y=0\): \(\log_2(x^2-3x-3)=0\). Since \(\log_2 1=0\), we need the argument to equal \(1\); then subtract \(1\) from both sides and factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2-3x-3 &= 1\\
x^2-3x-4 &= 0\\
(x-4)(x+1) &= 0
\end{aligned}
\]
So \(x=4\) or \(x=-1\). Both values make the argument positive: \((-1)^2-3(-1)-3=1>0\) and \(4^2-3(4)-3=1>0\). Therefore the \(x\)-intercepts are \((-1,0)\) and \((4,0)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Set the argument of the logarithm equal to \(1\), then solve the resulting quadratic equation.
